ov: Humped domestic cattle that originated in South Asia, with a fatty hump over the shoulders, a large dewlap and often drooping ears. Well adapted to heat and drought, they are raised throughout the tropics for draught work, milk, beef, hides and dung.

why.p: Small breeds such as the miniature zebu are kept as pets.
why.et: Raised for beef across the tropics; zebu breeds make up most of Brazil's beef cattle.

rg: Throughout the tropics: South Asia, China, Africa and Madagascar, and in large numbers in Brazil.
df: Grazes on grasses; it thrives on poor-quality forage.
fx: It was domesticated from the Indian aurochs 6,000–7,000 years ago at Mehrgarh, in what is now Pakistan.
